title: GitHub Actions policy step rules (.github/policy.rego): iterate step_entries(input) so composite-action and parallel steps are covered
answers: Why does my new conftest check for workflow steps not fire on steps inside a composite action.yml?
Which policy rule flags actions/github-script without retries or ${{ }} in its script, and how are its step locations reported?
How do I add a step-level check to the GitHub Actions policy that also covers parallel step groups?
body:
Path: .github/policy.rego:step_entries returns every step the step-level Conftest rules see: workflow jobs[].steps, parallel children, and composite-action runs.steps. It feeds token, checkout, create-github-app-token, github-script (retries, script interpolation), run-block interpolation, and step `if:` interpolation checks.
Rule: Step-level deny rules must iterate `some entry in step_entries(input)` with `step := entry.step`, not `input.jobs` or the old `job_steps(job)`. Report with `entry.location` (e.g. "job 'x', step #2", or the parallel/positional form) so unnamed steps are still locatable. Keep one rule per check; do not duplicate a workflow and a composite variant.
Symptom: Steps in composite actions (action.yml runs.steps) and parallel groups bypassed several step-level policy checks, because traversal was workflow-job-only and composite steps were handled by separate, partial duplicate rules.
Constraints: Job-level rules (e.g. job-level `if:` interpolation) do not go through step_entries. contains_github_token now guards with is_string(value), so non-string `with`/`env` values are skipped rather than erroring.
applies: Applies to .github/policy.rego step-level rules evaluated over workflow and composite action YAML; not to job-level or trigger-level rules.
says: My new Conftest step check does not fire on steps inside a composite action.yml file
Which policy check warns about actions/github-script without retries or with script interpolation, and where are step locations reported?
How do I make a new step-level GitHub Actions policy check also cover parallel step groups?
search: GitHub Actions policy step traversal: step-level deny rules must iterate the shared step_entries helper, which covers workflow job steps, parallel children and composite action steps, reporting the entry location. Job-level rules such as job if interpolation do not use it; avoid duplicate workflow and composite rules.
